newsitem.title: SPAIN: Four hurt in car bomb attack on Spanish barracks.
newsitem.headline: Four hurt in car bomb attack on Spanish barracks.

text.p: Four people were slightly injured when a car bomb exploded in front of Civil Guard barracks in the northeastern Spanish town of Bunuel, the local government of Navarre said on Friday.
Witnesses said a young man parked a Volkswagen, packed with explosives, near the barracks shortly after 1.00 a.m. (midnight GMT) and fled in another vehicle.
The parked car exploded shortly afterwards, blasting a ten-metre hole in the barracks wall and injuring three women and a Civil Guard. They did not require hospital treatment.
It was the sixth attack this year on the paramilitary Civil Guard's barracks in Navarre.

"We were sleeping in bed and all of a sudden, we heard a terrible noise," said the civil guard, a 31-year-old man whose three children were also sleeping in the barracks. "I saw a blast and the window crashed on top of me."

"The first thing I did was to get the children out of bed and bring them down into the street," said the man, who was not identified. "It isn't just luck, it's an authentic miracle (that more people were not injured)," he said.
The government's representative in the region, Francisco Javier Ansuategui, said on Friday the latest attack proved a commando of Basque separatist group ETA was active in the area.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed some 800 people since 1968 in its fight for an independent Basque state and frequently targets security forces and police.
